message.content:
**rs7412 (APOE) – allele frequency in European populations**

| Population group | rs7412 allele (T) frequency | rs7412 allele (C) frequency |
|------------------|-----------------------------|-----------------------------|
| **European (non‑Finnish)** – gnomAD v2.1.1 | **≈ 0.12 (12 %)** | ≈ 0.88 (88 %) |
| **European (Finnish)** – gnomAD v2.1.1 | ≈ 0.10 (10 %) | ≈ 0.90 (90 %) |
| **1000 Genomes Project – EUR (all sub‑populations)** | 0.11–0.13 (≈ 12 %) | 0.87–0.89 (≈ 88 %) |

> **Interpretation**  
> The T allele of rs7412 corresponds to the APOE ε2 allele, which is the “protective” allele for Alzheimer’s disease and is also associated with lower LDL‑cholesterol levels. In most European cohorts the T allele is present in roughly 10–15 % of chromosomes, with the exact value depending on the specific sub‑population (e.g., slightly lower in Finnish samples).

### Sources

1. **gnomAD v2.1.1** – *Allele frequency data for rs7412*  
   <https://gnomad.broadinstitute.org/variant/1-55516888-T-C>
2. **1000 Genomes Project** – *Population allele frequencies*  
   <https://www.internationalgenome.org/data-portal>

> **Note**  
> These figures represent *allele frequencies* (i.e., the proportion of all copies of the gene in the population that carry the T allele). If you need genotype frequencies (e.g., % of individuals who are TT, TC, or CC), you can approximate them using Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium:  
> - TT ≈ p²  
> - TC ≈ 2pq  
> - CC ≈ q²  
> where *p* = 0.12 (T allele frequency) and *q* = 0.88 (C allele frequency). This yields roughly 1.4 % TT, 21.1 % TC, and 77.5 % CC in a typical European cohort.

Feel free to let me know if you need the data broken down by a specific European sub‑population (e.g., British, Italian, etc.) or if you’d like genotype frequencies instead of allele frequencies.
